```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(cudaGlmnet)
```

`cudaGlmnet` fits the Gaussian lasso and elastic net with a glmnet-like
interface on top of the GPU FISTA solver in `rcupp`. This vignette covers the
lambda path, coefficient selection, cross-validation and `alpha` mixing.

## A lambda path

```{r path}
set.seed(1)
X <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 5), 60, 5)
y <- drop(X %*% c(2, -1, 0, 0, 0)) + rnorm(60, sd = 0.5)

fit <- cuda_glmnet(X, y, nlambda = 10)
length(fit$lambda)
fit$lambda[1:3]
```

By default the columns are scaled and an intercept is fitted; coefficients
are mapped back to the original scale. Select a penalty with the glmnet-style
`s` argument:

```{r coef}
coef(fit, s = fit$lambda[5])
predict(fit, X[1:3, ], s = fit$lambda[5])
```

## Cross-validation

```{r cv}
cv <- cv.cuda_glmnet(X, y, nlambda = 8, nfolds = 3)
cv$lambda.min
cv$lambda.1se
coef(cv, s = "lambda.1se")
```

`cv.cuda_glmnet()` returns the full path plus the cross-validated error, so
`coef()` and `predict()` accept the same `s` values as the plain fit.

## Elastic net and ridge

The `alpha` argument blends the lasso and ridge penalties in **glmnet's
convention**: `alpha = 1` (the default) is the lasso, `alpha = 0` is pure ridge,
and values in between give the elastic net, so `cuda_glmnet(X, y, lambda, alpha)`
reproduces `glmnet::glmnet(X, y, lambda, alpha)` (the internal lambda/alpha
remap is described in the `cuda_glmnet` help). For `alpha < 1` the solver loop is
composed downstream (Rcpp glue plus rcupp substrate) from rcupp's resident
device operators, with the design uploaded to the device once; rcupp itself
stays algorithm-agnostic. `enet_fista_cpu()` is the matching pure-R oracle for
the standard objective the solver uses internally (call it with the remapped
parameters to reproduce a fit).

```{r enet}
en <- cuda_glmnet(X, y, alpha = 0.5, nlambda = 10)
coef(en, s = en$lambda[5])
ridge <- cuda_glmnet(X, y, alpha = 0, nlambda = 6)
dim(ridge$beta)
```

## The reference path

For a single fixed penalty, `cuda_lasso()` calls the compiled solver once and
`lasso_fista_cpu()` is a dependency-free pure-R oracle that reproduces the
same numbers. Both are useful when checking the numerical contract.

```{r reference}
ref <- lasso_fista_cpu(X, y, lambda = 0.05)
head(ref$coefficients, 3)
```

The `glmnet-comparison` vignette checks that a `cuda_glmnet()` fit matches
`glmnet::glmnet()` for the Gaussian lasso, and the `glmnet-benchmark`
vignette measures their wall time on a shared lambda path. The
`gpu-lasso-comparison` vignette covers the third-party GPU solver and the
CUDA build notes in more detail.
